causalModel.founding: A tribeless Naga band camps on a bench below a pond. Two arms of the bone-road track meet at the bend below the bench. Every walker on the track must take that bend.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The camp stands on a low bench over a blind bend. Walkers on either arm of the track turn the pond's corner before they see the camp. The bank behind the bench drops to the flat. The drop gives the band a way out.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The band takes cargo and rarely kills. A robbed walker comes back next season. A dead walker brings his tribe against the camp.
causalModel.pressures: The settled tribes are blamed for the camp. The settled hold has begun paying the camp not to work its stretch. The hold would be ruined if the payment became known.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: A settlement between the settled and the tribeless would end the camp.

districts.notes: Two hide tents and a fire on a low bench over the bend of the track, a watch scaffold at its north edge, a cane gate where the track ends, held cargo behind the lieutenant's tent and grave cairns stepped down the bank.

why.what: The camp district holds two tents, the fire between them, the watch, the gate on the track and the held cargo.
why.whyHere: Both arms of the bone-road track bend round the pond and meet below this bench. Every walker on the track passes under the bench.
why.whySpot: The spot is the sole dry rise beside the bend. The bank falls away behind the rise.
why.whyNeighbours: The pond lies north of the bend. The flat south of the bank is empty marsh. The camp is out of sight of any dwelling.
why.playerPurpose: The camp is hostile and stops walkers at the bend. The band takes what walkers carry. The band cuts each walker a tally-stick for it.
why.microGeography: The camp stands on a low rise of firm ground in cypress marsh. The pond and the track bend lie to the north. A three-metre bank lies to the south.

districts.notes: The watch scaffold on the north-west corner of the bench, with the tally board hung under its platform.

why.what: The watch scaffold stands over the bend. The camp took its timber from a stockade that it robbed.
why.whyHere: From the corner of the bench a watcher can follow both arms of the track round the pond.
why.whySpot: The scaffold stands at the north-west corner of the bench. It stands above the west arm of the track.
why.whyNeighbours: The gate lies below the scaffold to the east. The fire lies behind the scaffold to the south-east.
why.playerPurpose: The scaffold is the lookout. A watcher on it sees a walker before the walker sees the camp.
why.microGeography: The scaffold stands on the north-west lip of the bench, above the track.

parcels.orientationWhy: The lieutenant's tent has its open front facing north-east. The open front faces the fire and, past the fire, the gate on the track.

why.what: The lieutenant's hide tent is the big tent. The held cargo is stacked behind it.
why.whyHere: The lieutenant keeps the tally and the claims. He sleeps where he can see the gate.
why.whySpot: The lieutenant's tent stands on the west half of the bench. Its back is to the bank.
why.whyNeighbours: The band's tent stands across the fire from the lieutenant's tent. The cargo and the cairns lie behind the lieutenant's tent. They are out of sight of the track.
why.playerPurpose: The lieutenant's tent is the lieutenant's post. Behind it is the cache of cargo that the camp holds against claims.
why.microGeography: The tent stands on the flat top of the bench. The ground there is trodden level.

parcels.orientationWhy: The band's tent has its open side facing north-west. The open side faces the fire.

why.what: The band's hide tent is where the rank and file sleep in turns.
why.whyHere: The band sleeps close to the fire and the gate.
why.whySpot: The band's tent stands on the east half of the bench. It faces the lieutenant's tent across the fire.
why.whyNeighbours: The band's tent stands across the fire from the lieutenant's tent. The band's own water and stores lie beside it.
why.playerPurpose: The band rests in the tent between turns at the gate.
why.microGeography: The tent stands at the east end of the bench. The ground there starts to fall to the flat.

parcels.orientationWhy: The watch scaffold stands at the north-west corner of the bench. It stands over the west arm of the track and the bend.

why.what: The watch scaffold has two stages and stands over the bend. The cane gate stands below it where the track ends.
why.whyHere: From the platform a watcher sees both arms of the track round the pond. The watcher sees them before the walkers see the camp.
why.whySpot: The scaffold stands at the north-west corner of the bench. That corner is the highest ground facing the track.
why.whyNeighbours: The gate stands on the track below the scaffold. The fire lies behind the scaffold.
why.playerPurpose: The scaffold is the lookout. The gate is where the camp stops walkers and cuts their tally.
why.microGeography: The scaffold stands on the north lip of the bench, above the bend of the track.

routes.why: A trodden way runs from the bend of the track through the gate and up the bench to the fire. It is the sole way into the camp.
A few steps lead from the camp path to the watch tower. The tally board hangs under the tower platform.
A mud yard runs round the fire. The ground is trodden bare between the lieutenant's tent and the band's tent.
The ground behind the lieutenant's tent is churned. The band drags crates and sacks in and out there.
The way out runs south, down the bank past the grave cairns to the flat.

approaches.sequence: A walker comes down the west arm of the track past the pond. The smoke shows first. Then the watch scaffold shows over the bend. Then the gate on the track shows, with the tents on the bench behind it.
approaches.wayfinding: The track bends round the pond to the gate. The camp path climbs from the gate to the fire.

approaches.sequence: A walker comes down the east arm of the track. The pond hides the bend until the last few metres. The band's tent shows on the bench. Then the gate shows across the track's end.
approaches.wayfinding: The east arm meets the west arm at the gate below the bench.

networkTerminals.why: The bone-road track's two arms meet at the bend below the bench. The camp path leaves the bend through the gate. The camp path climbs to the fire.

combatSpaces.why: The trodden ground round the fire lies between the two tents. It is level and open on the bench.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: The catalogue record The North Cut Camp is a camp of scale M1. It holds a lieutenant and a band of tribeless Naga.
scaleGrounding.why: A lieutenant and a band of four to seven fit two hide tents and a watch.

candidates.why: The candidate is the dry bench over the bend where both arms of the track meet below the pond. Tent pads there need cut and fill of at most 0.14 m.
The plotted anchor lies on the flat south of the bank.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The anchor lies 88 m south of the track. It sits below the bank and out of sight of the track. Its view covers nothing of the track.
